_schema: English mirror of szenen.json: same paths, string fields only (titel, schritte[].text for sag steps, ansprechen[], kommentar.text). Lists keep the German lengths; missing branches fall back to German. Barks are already English.

schritte.text: 'You said there'd be wifi.'
'I said there'd be sea.'
'The sea doesn't have wifi either.'
'Then I'm going diving. It's quiet down there.'
'That towel's been there since six, Harald! SIX!'
He comes back, wet, with a shell. She takes the shell. Ten seconds of peace.

ansprechen: She: 'Are you from the hotel? The wifi doesn't work.' He: 'Leave the boy, he sells sunglasses.' She: 'He doesn't have any sunglasses.' He: 'See, that's why the wifi doesn't work.'
Both at once: 'Do you have signal?' You don't. She: 'See.' He: 'YOU see.'
He, to you, quietly: 'Twenty years. Twenty. Got anything for ears?'

kommentar.text: 'The couple from the hotel was here. She wanted wifi, he wanted quiet. I gave them both an empty glass. Both happy.'

schritte.text: Three kids run in a circle. Not anywhere. In a circle.
'WAIT! MY SHOE!' Nobody waits.
The little one tips the bucket over whoever's nearest. Whoever's nearest is whoever's there.
The patrol walks through. The patrol trips over kid number two, who's looking for his shoe. The patrol gets up again, slowly, in sandals.
'POLICE! HANDS UP!' The kids have disarmed Pong. Pong wasn't carrying anything.

ansprechen: 'Got ice cream?' 'No.' 'Then what have you got?' '... nothing.' 'Then you're dumb.' They run on.
Kid three looks at you, looks at the bucket, looks at you. You take a step back. Correct.
'Mum says you're the guy who stands around on the beach.' 'Mum's right.' 'Mum's ALWAYS right.' Water pistol, right in the face.

kommentar.text: 'The kids knocked Pong over three times today. Three. The future of this island is in good, wet hands.'

schritte.text: Six a.m. A towel flies. Hits the lounger right at the front. That was the good one.
'The one next to it too. For the Müllers.'
Second towel. Third. Fourth. The Müllers arrive at two.
'Seven. That's enough. Breakfast.' They leave. The loungers stay empty until two in the afternoon.

ansprechen: 'That one's reserved.' You didn't say anything. 'That one too.'
He, without looking at you: 'We were here first. Yesterday too. And the day before.' She: 'And tomorrow.'
'Do you have a towel? No? Then you don't have a lounger either. That's how it's regulated.'

schritte.text: 'BANGKOK, BABY! Best city in the world!' Nong doesn't correct him. Nong never corrects anyone.
'I love this city. Where's the beach? Is this the beach? Bangkok has a BEACH?'
He tips backwards. He catches himself. He celebrates having caught himself.
'Chef! Chef, you're my best friend here.' The seagull looks at him like a french fry.
From six p.m. he sleeps on the counter. From eight, in your hammock.

ansprechen: 'Bro! BRO! You know where we are?' 'Bangi Bay.' 'BANGKOK Bay! Knew it.'
'Have you got... you know... I'm in BANGKOK, man, they've got EVERYTHING here.' He has no money left. He had money. Chef has it.
'My flight's tomorrow. From Bangkok. Which way is Bangkok from here?' You point at the sea. He nods. 'Thought so.'

kommentar.text: 'The American is sleeping in your hammock. He thinks this is Bangkok. Let him. In Bangkok he'd have been robbed by now.'

schritte.text: 'One more. The light was just perfect.' It's twelve noon. The light has been the same for hours.
He lifts the reflector. The reflector is as big as he is. He used to be bigger than the reflector, on the inside.
Click. Click. Click. 'Sunset in Bangi, hashtag blessed.'
He looks at the sea. The sea looks back. Neither says anything.
'A bit to the left. No, YOUR left.' He goes right. It's correct. It's always the wrong thing that's correct.

ansprechen: She, without looking at you: 'Can you get out of the shot? Thanks. You're in it. Still. Thanks.'
He, quietly: 'She's got 40,000 followers. I'm one of them. I never confirmed it.'
'Are you local? Do something local in the background.' You stand there. It's the most local thing you've got.

schritte.text: One p.m. Pong puts his feet on the desk, cap over his face. The board says: 'Lunch break. Incidents from 2 p.m.'
Snoring. The whistle on its cord rises and falls with his belly.
In his sleep he whistles once. Briefly. Nobody knows who he's dreaming about.
Two p.m. Pong wakes up, puts the cap on, flips the board: 'Days without incident: {tage}'. The patrol walks again.

ansprechen: You stand in front of Pong. Pong is asleep. You could do anything. You do nothing. That's the difference between you and Timo.
Pong, from under the cap: 'I'm asleep. No incident. Go.' He really is asleep. He says it in his sleep.
The mango from this morning is on the desk. Half eaten. Pong is dreaming about the other half.

schritte.text: A guy in a bandana sneaks across the beach as if sneaking were normal. He carries his sandals on his belt. Barefoot counts as harmless, he knows that.
The woman on the lounger is asleep. Bag next to the lounger, open, wallet on top. She's dreaming of wifi.
Grab, bag, gone. He even picks up the woman's sunglasses that were lying next to it and puts them back. Manners.
'MY BAG!' She's awake. She's very awake.
He runs. Barefoot. Faster than anything wearing shoes around here. Waves backwards while he does it.
Pong whistles, Pong gives chase. Pong in sandals behind a barefoot man. The result is settled, but the patrol is gone for a while. That's your window.

ansprechen: You talk to the thief before he steals. He grins: 'Colleague. You do your business, I do mine. Or you want to call Pong? He's got sandals. Like you.'
You whistle him on to Pong. Pong doesn't get him, but he remembers you helped. Today he looks away once.
The woman on the lounger, still half asleep: 'Are you the lounger service? Another towel, then.'

schritte.text: The bandana guy again. Today he's got a victim with a camera in his sights. The camera hangs on the neck, the neck hangs on the tourist, the tourist hangs on his phone.
The tourist is photographing a bin. With flash. He's taken 300 photos today. Of bins, signs and you.
One grab, the strap is open (it already was; the tourist is German and careful, but not with straps). Camera gone. The thief takes a selfie on the way.
'MY CAMERA! The bins were on there!'
He runs towards the market, where you vanish in the crowd. He knows what you know.
Pong gives chase, whistling, in sandals. The patrol is busy for a while. Your window.

ansprechen: The thief, to you, without slowing down: 'Camera? Don't want it. Just want him to look for it. Look at him looking!'
You point Pong in the right direction. Pong nods gratefully and runs in the wrong one. Still counts.
The tourist, to you: 'Did you see that? Can you testify? Do you have a photo?' You have none of those.
